Maintain appropriate confidentiality of discussions, documents and correspondence handled through the CFO Office. Maturity – comfortable interacting with senior executives and external stakeholders. Learning agility – quickly develops an understanding of the business and the CFO's priorities. Composure – remains effective in a fast-paced and demanding environment. What Success Looks Like The EA to CFO should progressively become a trusted extension of the CFO Office—someone who ensures that the CFO's time is focused on the highest-value priorities, important matters do not fall through the cracks, meetings translate into action, and relevant information reaches the CFO in a concise and decision-ready form.
